behavior: DynamicArrayCachedIterator stores actual current and block-end pointers alongside the existing detached position state. It does not synthesize element addresses from logical IDs, copy the owner block table, or dereference the stored owner pointer.

Shared construction captures read provenance from block.as_ptr. Mutable construction/reload captures writable raw provenance directly from block.as_mut_ptr, covering the block rather than narrowing to a single &mut T. Const conversion and Clone copy the real cached pointers without reloading. No Clone/Default bound is imposed on payload T.

Pointer getters return the actual saved address, More tests null, and same_position compares original container identity plus index independently of pointer equality. Unsafe value/change_value require initialized current storage, allocation-owner lifetime, retained pointer provenance and appropriate shared/exclusive access.

Checked advance/retreat/offset accept the original owner explicitly and verify its address before changing state. Within-block increments preserve the transferred pointer; native boundary reloads and even offset0 consult the original container. Failed reload/owner/overflow validation leaves the saved state unchanged.

Thirteen native rows prove move construction and move Assign preserve cached pointer identity and writable access in the destination while iterator equality still names the original source. After source refill, cached value2 remains from the old block, offset0 selects source102, crossing the old boundary selects source103, and retreat selects source102.

A native row and strict Miri show cached reads remain valid after destruction of the original container when the moved-to array retains the allocation. Such access never reads owner metadata. Further navigation requires an available original owner reference and is intentionally a narrower domain.

Tests cover shared and mutable pointer transfer, non-Clone payload writes, const traversal across blocks, exhausted-pointer return, const conversion, copied cursor state, wrong owners, absent/dead-slot reloads, signed overflow and rejecting null-pointer increments after unsigned index wrap.

All52 original runtime names join normal and strict Miri logs. Existing safe detached cursor behavior is unchanged. The receipt contains23 exact inventory IDs including distinct template and callable child declarations; they are scoped partial bindings, not23 newly completed semantic APIs. Const-specialized navigation bodies are distinguished by full compiler impl_context literal false/true.
limitations: This is an explicit cached-pointer adapter, not a replacement of every existing safe iterator convenience. Remaining cached postfix, arithmetic-returning-copy, subscript, difference/order, assignment and legacy Init/Initialize surfaces are not claimed complete by this batch.

Safe navigation may compute or return a raw address for an ended or invalidated element; More/pointer are not lifetime validation. Actual dereference is unsafe and callers must keep the current allocation alive and avoid conflicting access. No read of a dead slot is tested or authorized.

Navigation requires a supplied original owner even in native phases that do not read it. After original-owner destruction, cached pointer/value observations are supported under their lifetime contract, but navigation cannot be expressed through this checked adapter.

Wrong-owner and invalid initialized-slot/block-end checks, signed-overflow errors and null-increment rejection are Rust boundary extensions outside defined native dereference/navigation cases. Zero-sized payloads, zero-stride retained mutation and incompatible retained block-end layouts remain outside captured slot domains.
C++ cached-pointer semantics do not remove Rust provenance obligations. A pointer whose tag was invalidated by a conflicting Rust reference is not made valid by container transfer or by this adapter.

Native generic overload bindings cover default IsConstant-dependent enable_if parameters; explicit unusual template-parameter overrides and virtual legacy cursor override behavior are not proved. Cross-platform ABI/layout and native dangling-pointer reads remain excluded.
Public copy-constructor failure descriptor-unwind and leaked resource lifetimes remain actionable in the separate copy-policy work; this iterator adapter does not change that domain.
validation_scope: Final source passes20 DynamicArray integration targets (284 tests),21 units, strict Clippy/fmt and103 strict Miri tests. One native probe compiles with UBSan; linked TKernel is prebuilt.23 exact native declarations bind body-bearing Rust cached-pointer methods, with both specialized navigation signatures identified by const impl context. No shared ledger or raw lifetime helper changes.
